_meta.title: Genesis — key verses (King James Version, public domain)
_meta.description: Several curated key verses from Genesis (creation, covenant, promise, and the pivotal patriarch/Joseph narratives). Ecosystem-generic 864zeros content. Each record carries the exact scripture plus an original plain-English rendering.
_meta.license: Public domain (KJV scripture); 'plain' renderings are original 864zeros writing
_meta.source: getbible.net v2 (KJV, book 1 Genesis); verses verbatim, curly apostrophes normalized to straight, proper-name en-dashes to hyphens
_meta.selection: several key verses per substantive chapter; pure-genealogy and graphic-only narrative chapters are omitted (37 of 50 chapters represented)
_meta.keying: book + chapter + citation; multiple records per chapter
_meta.renderings: text = the exact KJV verse; plain = original 864zeros plain-English 2026 rendering, faithful to the verse's meaning (~grade 6-8), authored not quoted.
_meta.note: getbible's KJV renders the divine name as 'the Lord'; text is verbatim KJV. No review gate — author is reviewer.

verses.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
verses.plain: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

verses.text: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
verses.plain: So God created humankind in his own image; in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.

verses.text: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.
verses.plain: God saw all that he had made, and it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning — the sixth day.

verses.text: And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
verses.plain: Then the Lord God formed the man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living being.

verses.text: And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
verses.plain: The Lord God said, 'It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.'

verses.text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
verses.plain: That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife, and the two become one flesh.

verses.text: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
verses.plain: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.

verses.text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
verses.plain: By the sweat of your brow you will eat your food until you return to the ground, since from it you were taken; for dust you are, and to dust you will return.

verses.text: If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.
verses.plain: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not, sin is crouching at your door; it desires to have you, but you must rule over it.

verses.text: And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's keeper?
verses.plain: Then the Lord said to Cain, 'Where is your brother Abel?' 'I don't know,' he replied. 'Am I my brother's keeper?'

verses.text: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.
verses.plain: Enoch walked faithfully with God; then he was no more, because God took him away.

verses.text: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.
verses.plain: But Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord.

verses.text: These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.
verses.plain: This is the account of Noah: Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked faithfully with God.

verses.text: And they that went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him: and the Lord shut him in.
verses.plain: The animals going in were male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the Lord shut him in.

verses.text: While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.
verses.plain: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease.

verses.text: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
verses.plain: I have set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth.

verses.text: Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the Lord did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the Lord scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
verses.plain: That is why it was called Babel — because there the Lord confused the language of the whole world, and from there he scattered them over all the earth.

verses.text: Now the Lord had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee:
verses.plain: The Lord had said to Abram, 'Leave your country, your people, and your father's household, and go to the land I will show you.'

verses.text: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:
verses.plain: I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing.

verses.text: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
verses.plain: I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse; and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you.

verses.text: For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.
verses.plain: All the land that you see I will give to you and your offspring forever.

verses.text: And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth:
verses.plain: and he blessed him, saying, 'Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.'

verses.text: After these things the word of the Lord came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward.
verses.plain: After this, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision: 'Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.'

verses.text: And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.
verses.plain: Abram believed the Lord, and he credited it to him as righteousness.

verses.text: And she called the name of the Lord that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?
verses.plain: She gave this name to the Lord who spoke to her: 'You are the God who sees me,' for she said, 'I have now seen the One who sees me.'

verses.text: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, the Lord appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.
verses.plain: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to him and said, 'I am God Almighty; walk before me faithfully and be blameless.'

verses.text: And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee.
verses.plain: I will establish my covenant as an everlasting covenant between me and you and your descendants after you, to be your God and the God of your descendants after you.

verses.text: Is any thing too hard for the Lord? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.
verses.plain: Is anything too hard for the Lord? At the appointed time I will return to you, and Sarah will have a son.

verses.text: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
verses.plain: But Lot's wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.

verses.text: And God said unto him in a dream, Yea, I know that thou didst this in the integrity of thy heart; for I also withheld thee from sinning against me: therefore suffered I thee not to touch her.
verses.plain: Then God said to him in the dream, 'Yes, I know you did this with a clear conscience, and so I have kept you from sinning against me.'

verses.text: And the Lord visited Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did unto Sarah as he had spoken.
verses.plain: Now the Lord was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did for Sarah what he had promised.

verses.text: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
verses.plain: Abraham answered, 'God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.' And the two of them went on together.

verses.text: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the Lord it shall be seen.
verses.plain: So Abraham called that place The Lord Will Provide. And to this day it is said, 'On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.'

verses.text: And he said, Blessed be the Lord God of my master Abraham, who hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I being in the way, the Lord led me to the house of my master's brethren.
verses.plain: saying, 'Blessed be the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who has not abandoned his kindness and faithfulness to my master. As for me, the Lord has led me on the journey.'

verses.text: And Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren: and the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
verses.plain: Isaac prayed to the Lord on behalf of his wife, because she was childless. The Lord answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant.

verses.text: And the Lord appeared unto him the same night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham's sake.
verses.plain: That night the Lord appeared to him and said, 'I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you; I will bless you.'

verses.text: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.
verses.plain: I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.

verses.text: And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the Lord is in this place; and I knew it not.
verses.plain: When Jacob awoke from his sleep, he thought, 'Surely the Lord is in this place, and I was not aware of it.'

verses.text: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.
verses.plain: So Jacob served seven years to marry Rachel, but they seemed like only a few days to him because of his love for her.

verses.text: And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb.
verses.plain: Then God remembered Rachel; he listened to her and enabled her to conceive.

verses.text: And Mizpah; for he said, The Lord watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.
verses.plain: It was also called Mizpah, because he said, 'May the Lord keep watch between you and me when we are away from each other.'

verses.text: And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.
verses.plain: Then the man said, 'Let me go, for it is daybreak.' But Jacob replied, 'I will not let you go unless you bless me.'

verses.text: And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.
verses.plain: Then the man said, 'Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with people and have overcome.'

verses.text: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.
verses.plain: But Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept.

verses.text: And let us arise, and go up to Beth-el; and I will make there an altar unto God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.
verses.plain: Then come, let us go up to Bethel, where I will build an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress and who has been with me wherever I have gone.

verses.text: And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
verses.plain: The Lord was with Joseph, so that he prospered, and he lived in the house of his Egyptian master.

verses.text: But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
verses.plain: But the Lord was with Joseph and showed him kindness, and granted him favor in the eyes of the prison warden.

verses.text: And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.
verses.plain: 'We both had dreams,' they answered, 'but there is no one to interpret them.' Then Joseph said, 'Don't interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.'

verses.text: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
verses.plain: 'I cannot do it,' Joseph replied to Pharaoh, 'but God will give Pharaoh the answer he desires.'

verses.text: And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?
verses.plain: So Pharaoh asked his officials, 'Can we find anyone like this man, one in whom is the Spirit of God?'

verses.text: Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.
verses.plain: And now, do not be distressed or angry with yourselves for selling me here, because it was to save lives that God sent me ahead of you.

verses.text: And God sent me before you to preserve you a posterity in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
verses.plain: But God sent me ahead of you to preserve a remnant on earth and to save your lives by a great deliverance.

verses.text: I have waited for thy salvation, O Lord.
verses.plain: I wait for your salvation, Lord.

verses.text: But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.
verses.plain: You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good, to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives.

verses.text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
verses.plain: Then Joseph said to his brothers, 'I am about to die. But God will surely come to your aid and take you up out of this land to the land he promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.'
